sanskrit: rājā prabhaṃkaro nāma kule asmin babhūva ha aputraḥ prasavenārthī tapas tepe sa uttamam
english: In this lineage there was a king named Prabhankara who, childless and longing for offspring, performed the most arduous austerities.

sanskrit: ugreṇa tapasā tena praṇipātena śaṃkaraḥ īśvaras toṣitas tena mahādeva umāpatiḥ
english: By that fierce austerity and prostration, Shankara, the Lord Mahādeva, husband of Umā, was pleased by him.

sanskrit: sa tasmai bhagavān prādād ekaikaṃ prasavaṃ kule ekaikaḥ prasavas tasmād bhavaty asmin kule sadā
english: The Blessed Lord granted him one birth in the lineage; and since then, only one birth at a time has ever occurred in this family.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ kumārāḥ sarveṣāṃ pūrveṣāṃ mama jajñire kanyā tu mama jāteyaṃ kulasyotpādanī dhruvam
english: From all those earlier ancestors of mine, only boys were born; but this daughter of mine was born as the certain perpetuator of the lineage.

sanskrit: putro mameyam iti me bhāvanā puruṣottama putrikā hetuvidhinā saṃjñitā bharatarṣabha
english: My conviction is that she is my son, O best of men; by the rule of the putrika she is designated thus, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: etac chulkaṃ bhavatv asyāḥ kulakṛj jāyatām iha etena samayenemāṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva pāṇḍava
english: Let this be the bride-price for her: a son born here shall be the founder of the lineage. On this condition accept her, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: sa tatheti pratijñāya kanyāṃ tāṃ pratigṛhya ca uvāsa nagare tasmin kaunteyas trihimāḥ samāḥ
english: Having pledged "so be it" and having accepted that maiden, the son of Kuntī dwelt in that city for three winter seasons.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ samudre tīrthāni dakṣiṇe bharatarṣabhaḥ abhyagacchat supuṇyāni śobhitāni tapasvibhiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the bull of the Bharatas proceeded to visit the most sacred shrines on the southern ocean, adorned by ascetics.

sanskrit: varjayanti sma tīrthāni pañca tatra tu tāpasāḥ ācīrṇāni tu yāny āsan purastāt tu tapasvibhiḥ
english: The ascetics there avoided five of those shrines — those which had previously been frequented by ascetics of old.

sanskrit: agastyatīrthaṃ saubhadraṃ paulomaṃ ca supāvanam kāraṃdhamaṃ prasannaṃ ca hayamedhaphalaṃ ca yat bhāradvājasya tīrthaṃ ca pāpapraśamanaṃ mahat
english: Agastya's shrine, Saubhadra, Pauloma — most purifying — Karandhama the clear, the one granting the fruit of the horse-sacrifice, and the great shrine of Bharadvaja that quells sin.

sanskrit: viviktāny upalakṣyātha tāni tīrthāni pāṇḍavaḥ dṛṣṭvā ca varjyamānāni munibhir dharmabuddhibhiḥ
english: The Pāṇḍava noticed those shrines to be deserted, and seeing them shunned by the sages of righteous mind,

sanskrit: tapasvinas tato 'pṛcchat prājñaliḥ kurunandanaḥ tīrthānīmāni varjyante kimarthaṃ brahmavādibhiḥ
english: the descendant of Kuru then asked the ascetics with folded hands: "Why are these shrines avoided by those versed in sacred lore?"

sanskrit: tāpasā ūcuḥ grāhāḥ pañca vasanty eṣu haranti ca tapodhanān ata etāni varjyante tīrthāni kurunandana
english: The ascetics said: Five crocodiles dwell in these waters and drag down men rich in austerity; therefore these shrines are avoided, O descendant of Kuru.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca teṣāṃ śrutvā mahābāhur vāryamāṇas tapodhanaiḥ jagāma tāni tīrthāni draṣṭuṃ puruṣasattamaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing their words, the mighty-armed best of men — though restrained by the ascetics — went to see those shrines himself.

sanskrit: tataḥ saubhadram āsādya maharṣes tīrtham uttamam vigāhya tarasā śūraḥ snānaṃ cakre paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then reaching Saubhadra, the foremost shrine of the great sage, the heroic scorcher of foes plunged in swiftly and bathed.

sanskrit: atha taṃ puruṣavyāghram antarjalacaro mahān nijagrāha jale grāhaḥ kuntīputraṃ dhanaṃjayam
english: Then a great crocodile dwelling beneath the water seized in the depths that tiger among men, Dhanañjaya, son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: sa tam ādāya kaunteyo visphurantaṃ jalecaram udatiṣṭhan mahābāhur balena balināṃ varaḥ
english: The mighty-armed son of Kuntī, best among the strong, lifted that thrashing water-creature out of the water by sheer force.

sanskrit: utkṛṣṭa eva tu grāhaḥ so 'rjunena yaśasvinā babhūva nārī kalyāṇī sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā dīpyamānā śriyā rājan divyarūpā manoramā
english: As it was dragged out by the glorious Arjuna, the crocodile became a beautiful woman adorned with all ornaments, blazing with splendour, O king — divine in form and enchanting to behold.

sanskrit: tad adbhutaṃ mahad dṛṣṭvā kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ tāṃ striyaṃ paramaprīta idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Seeing that great marvel, Dhanañjaya, son of Kuntī, was utterly delighted and spoke these words to that woman:

sanskrit: kā vai tvam asi kalyāṇi kuto vāsi jalecarī kimarthaṃ ca mahat pāpam idaṃ kṛtavatī purā
english: "Who are you, fair one? Where do you come from, you who were dwelling in the water? And why did you formerly commit this great sin?"

sanskrit: nāry uvāca apsarāsmi mahābāho devāraṇyavicāriṇī iṣṭā dhanapater nityaṃ vargā nāma mahābala
english: The woman said: I am an apsara, O mighty-armed one, who roams the divine forests; I am beloved of the Lord of wealth — Varga is my name, O great one.

sanskrit: mama sakhyaś catasro 'nyāḥ sarvāḥ kāmagamāḥ śubhāḥ tābhiḥ sārdhaṃ prayātāsmi lokapālaniveśanam
english: I have four other companions, all beautiful and able to go wherever they wish; together with them I had journeyed to the abode of the World-guardians.

sanskrit: tataḥ paśyāmahe sarvā brāhmaṇaṃ saṃśitavratam rūpavantam adhīyānam ekam ekāntacāriṇam
english: There we all beheld a brahmin firm in his vow, handsome, engaged in study, alone, wandering in solitude.

sanskrit: tasya vai tapasā rājaṃs tad vanaṃ tejasāvṛtam āditya iva taṃ deśaṃ kṛtsnaṃ sa vyavabhāsayat
english: By his austerity, O king, that entire forest was covered with his radiance; like the sun, he illumined that whole region.

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvā tapas tādṛg rūpaṃ cādbhutadarśanam avatīrṇāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ tapovighnacikīrṣayā
english: Seeing such austerity and a form so wondrous to behold, we descended to that place intending to obstruct his penances.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca saurabheyī ca samīcī budbudā latā yaugapadyena taṃ vipram abhyagacchāma bhārata
english: I, and Saurabheyī, Samici, Budbuda, and Lata — all together we approached that brahmin, O Bharata.

sanskrit: gāyantyo vai hasantyaś ca lobhayantyaś ca taṃ dvijam sa ca nāsmāsu kṛtavān mano vīra kathaṃ cana nākampata mahātejāḥ sthitas tapasi nirmale
english: Singing, laughing, and enticing that twice-born, he did not at all turn his mind toward us, O hero; the great-souled one did not waver, established in pure austerity.

sanskrit: so 'śapat kupito 'smāṃs tu brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyarṣabha grāhabhūtā jale yūyaṃ cariṣyadhvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ
english: That brahmin, angered, cursed us, O bull among warriors: 'You shall become crocodiles and roam the waters for a hundred years.'

sanskrit: vargovāca tato vayaṃ pravyathitāḥ sarvā bharatasattama āyāma śaraṇaṃ vipraṃ taṃ tapodhanam acyutam
english: Varga said: Then all of us, greatly distressed, O best of the Bharatas, went for refuge to that unwavering brahmin rich in austerity.

sanskrit: rūpeṇa vayasā caiva kandarpeṇa ca darpitāḥ ayuktaṃ kṛtavatyaḥ sma kṣantum arhasi no dvija
english: 'Intoxicated by beauty, youth, and the arrows of Kāma, we have done what was not fitting; please forgive us, O twice-born one.'

sanskrit: eṣa eva vadho 'smākaṃ suparyāptas tapodhana yad vayaṃ saṃśitātmānaṃ pralobdhuṃ tvām ihāgatāḥ
english: 'This itself is punishment enough for us, O wealth of austerity, that we came here to tempt you, a man of sharpened soul.'

sanskrit: avadhyās tu striyaḥ sṛṣṭā manyante dharmacintakāḥ tasmād dharmeṇa dharmajña nāsmān hiṃsitum arhasi
english: 'Those who contemplate the law hold that women were created inviolable; therefore by the law, O knower of the law, you ought not to harm us.'

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣu dharmajña maitro brāhmaṇa ucyate satyo bhavatu kalyāṇa eṣa vādo manīṣiṇām
english: 'A brahmin is called the friend of all beings, O knower of the law; may this saying of the wise prove true, O auspicious one.'

sanskrit: śaraṇaṃ ca prapannānāṃ śiṣṭāḥ kurvanti pālanam śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ prapannāḥ sma tasmāt tvaṃ kṣantum arhasi
english: 'The righteous protect those who come to them for refuge; we have come to you for refuge, therefore you ought to forgive us.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu dharmātmā brāhmaṇaḥ śubhakarmakṛt prasādaṃ kṛtavān vīra ravisomasamaprabhaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, that righteous brahmin, doer of auspicious deeds, radiant as the sun and moon combined, was gracious, O hero.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca śataṃ sahasraṃ viśvaṃ ca sarvam akṣayavācakam parimāṇaṃ śataṃ tv etan naitad akṣayavācakam
english: The brahmin said: A hundred, a thousand, the all — these words denote the inexhaustible; but "hundred" here is merely a measure and does not mean the inexhaustible.

sanskrit: yadā ca vo grāhabhūtā gṛhṇantīḥ puruṣāñ jale utkarṣati jalāt kaś cit sthalaṃ puruṣasattamaḥ
english: When you, having become crocodiles, are seizing men in the water, and some best of men lifts one of you from the water to dry land —

sanskrit: tadā yūyaṃ punaḥ sarvāḥ svarūpaṃ pratipatsyatha anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me hasatāpi kadā cana
english: then you shall all regain your own forms. Never before have I spoken an untruth, even in jest.

sanskrit: tāni sarvāṇi tīrthāni itaḥ prabhṛti caiva ha nārītīrthāni nāmneha khyātiṃ yāsyanti sarvaśaḥ puṇyāni ca bhaviṣyanti pāvanāni manīṣiṇām
english: All those shrines from this time forward shall everywhere be known in the world as the Women's Shrines by name, and shall be holy and purifying for the wise.

sanskrit: vargovāca tato 'bhivādya taṃ vipraṃ kṛtvā caiva pradakṣiṇam acintayāmopasṛtya tasmād deśāt suduḥkhitāḥ
english: Varga said: Then, having saluted that brahmin and circumambulated him, we departed from that region in great distress, pondering our fate.

sanskrit: kva nu nāma vayaṃ sarvāḥ kālenālpena taṃ naram samāgacchema yo nas tad rūpam āpādayet punaḥ
english: "Where indeed and when shall we all meet that man who will restore us to our own forms once more?"

sanskrit: tā vayaṃ cintayitvaivaṃ muhūrtād iva bhārata dṛṣṭavatyo mahābhāgaṃ devarṣim uta nāradam
english: While we were pondering thus, O Bharata, in a moment as it were, we caught sight of the greatly blessed divine sage Nārada.

sanskrit: sarvā hṛṣṭāḥ sma taṃ dṛṣṭvā devarṣim amitadyutim abhivādya ca taṃ pārtha sthitāḥ sma vyathitānanāḥ
english: All of us were delighted to see that divine sage of immeasurable brilliance; we saluted him, O Pārtha, and stood before him with anguished faces.

sanskrit: sa no 'pṛcchad duḥkhamūlam uktavatyo vayaṃ ca tat śrutvā tac ca yathāvṛttam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He asked us the root of our suffering; we told him everything; and having heard it and the entire occurrence, he spoke these words:

sanskrit: dakṣiṇe sāgarānūpe pañca tīrthāni santi vai puṇyāni ramaṇīyāni tāni gacchata māciram
english: 'On the southern shore of the ocean there are five sacred and delightful shrines — go there without delay.'

sanskrit: tatrāśu puruṣavyāghraḥ pāṇḍavo vo dhanaṃjayaḥ mokṣayiṣyati śuddhātmā duḥkhād asmān na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'There soon the tiger among men, the Pāṇḍava Dhanañjaya, pure of soul, will without doubt rescue you from your suffering.'

sanskrit: tasya sarvā vayaṃ vīra śrutvā vākyam ihāgatāḥ tad idaṃ satyam evādya mokṣitāhaṃ tvayānagha
english: Hearing his words, all of us came here, O hero; and today that has come true — I have been freed by you, O sinless one.

sanskrit: etās tu mama vai sakhyaś catasro 'nyā jale sthitāḥ kuru karma śubhaṃ vīra etāḥ sarvā vimokṣaya
english: These four other companions of mine still remain in the water; perform a good deed, O hero — free them all.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tāḥ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaḥ sarvā eva viśāṃ pate tasmāc chāpād adīnātmā mokṣayām āsa vīryavān
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the foremost of Pāṇḍavas, lord of the people, undaunted in spirit, the valiant one, freed them all from that curse.

sanskrit: utthāya ca jalāt tasmāt pratilabhya vapuḥ svakam tās tadāpsaraso rājann adṛśyanta yathā purā
english: Rising from that water and regaining their own forms, those apsaras, O king, became visible again just as they had been before.

sanskrit: tīrthāni śodhayitvā tu tathānujñāya tāḥ prabhuḥ citrāṅgadāṃ punar draṣṭuṃ maṇalūrapuraṃ yayau
english: Having thus purified those shrines and taken leave of them, the lord went to the city of Manalura to see Citrāṅgada again.

sanskrit: tasyām ajanayat putraṃ rājānaṃ babhruvāhanam taṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavo rājan gokarṇam abhito 'gamat
english: Upon her he fathered a son, the king Babhruvāhana; having seen him, O king, the Pāṇḍava proceeded toward Gokarṇa.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca so 'parānteṣu tīrthāni puṇyāny āyatanāni ca sarvāṇy evānupūrvyeṇa jagāmāmitavikramaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: He of immeasurable prowess visited in due order all the sacred shrines and holy places in the western coastal region.

sanskrit: samudre paścime yāni tīrthāny āyatanāni ca tāni sarvāṇi gatvā sa prabhāsam upajagmivān
english: Having visited all the shrines and holy places on the western ocean, he arrived at Prabhāsa.

sanskrit: prabhāsadeśaṃ saṃprāptaṃ bībhatsum aparājitam tīrthāny anucarantaṃ ca śuśrāva madhusūdanaḥ
english: The slayer of Madhu heard that Bībhatsu, the unconquered, had reached the Prabhāsa region and was travelling from shrine to shrine.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyagacchat kaunteyam ajñāto nāma mādhavaḥ dadṛśāte tadānyonyaṃ prabhāse kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau
english: Then the Mādhava went unannounced to the son of Kuntī; and the two — Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava — beheld each other at Prabhāsa.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ samāśliṣya pṛṣṭvā ca kuśalaṃ vane āstāṃ priyasakhāyau tau naranārāyaṇāv ṛṣī
english: The two dear friends — those seers Nara and Nārāyaṇa — embraced one another and enquired after each other's welfare in the forest, and sat down together.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ vāsudevas tāṃ caryāṃ paryapṛcchata kimarthaṃ pāṇḍavemāni tīrthāny anucarasy uta
english: Then Vāsudeva asked Arjuna about that journey: "Why, O Pāṇḍava, do you travel through all these shrines?"

sanskrit: tato 'rjuno yathāvṛttaṃ sarvam ākhyātavāṃs tadā śrutvovāca ca vārṣṇeya evam etad iti prabhuḥ
english: Then Arjuna narrated everything as it had occurred; and hearing it, the lord of the Vṛṣṇi clan said "Even so it is."

sanskrit: tau vihṛtya yathākāmaṃ prabhāse kṛṣṇapāṇḍavau mahīdharaṃ raivatakaṃ vāsāyaivābhijagmatuḥ
english: After the two — Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍava — had taken their pleasure at Prabhāsa as they wished, they went to the mountain Raivataka to spend the night.

sanskrit: pūrvam eva tu kṛṣṇasya vacanāt taṃ mahīdharam puruṣāḥ samalaṃcakrur upajahruś ca bhojanam
english: At Kṛṣṇa's prior instruction, men had already adorned that mountain and brought food there.

sanskrit: pratigṛhyārjunaḥ sarvam upabhujya ca pāṇḍavaḥ sahaiva vāsudevena dṛṣṭavān naṭanartakān
english: Arjuna accepted everything, and the Pāṇḍava, having enjoyed it together with Vāsudeva, watched actors and dancers.

sanskrit: abhyanujñāpya tān sarvān arcayitvā ca pāṇḍavaḥ satkṛtaṃ śayanaṃ divyam abhyagacchan mahādyutiḥ
english: Having dismissed them all and honoured them, the Pāṇḍava of great radiance went to a well-appointed, divine bed.

sanskrit: tīrthānāṃ darśanaṃ caiva parvatānāṃ ca bhārata āpagānāṃ vanānāṃ ca kathayām āsa sātvate
english: He recounted to the Sātvata the sights of the shrines, the mountains, the rivers, and the forests, O Bharata.

sanskrit: sa kathāḥ kathayann eva nidrayā janamejaya kaunteyo 'pahṛtas tasmiñ śayane svargasaṃmite
english: While still telling those tales, O Janamejaya, the son of Kuntī was carried away by sleep on that heaven-like bed.

sanskrit: madhureṇa sa gītena vīṇāśabdena cānagha prabodhyamāno bubudhe stutibhir maṅgalais tathā
english: Roused by sweet song and the sound of the vina, and by auspicious hymns of praise, O sinless one, he awoke.

sanskrit: sa kṛtvāvaśyakāryāṇi vārṣṇeyenābhinanditaḥ rathena kāñcanāṅgena dvārakām abhijagmivān
english: Having performed his necessary duties and welcomed by the Vṛṣṇi lord, he set out for Dvārakā on a chariot with golden fittings.

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtā dvārakā tu babhūva janamejaya kuntīsutasya pūjārtham api niṣkuṭakeṣv api
english: Dvārakā was adorned, O Janamejaya, in honour of the son of Kuntī — even in the inner courtyards.

sanskrit: didṛkṣavaś ca kaunteyaṃ dvārakāvāsino janāḥ narendramārgam ājagmus tūrṇaṃ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: The people of Dvārakā, eager to see the son of Kuntī, rushed in hundreds of thousands to the king's highway.

sanskrit: avalokeṣu nārīṇāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni ca bhojavṛṣṇyandhakānāṃ ca samavāyo mahān abhūt
english: At the viewing-galleries there were hundreds and thousands of women, and a great assembly of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas gathered.

sanskrit: sa tathā satkṛtaḥ sarvair bhojavṛṣṇyandhakātmajaiḥ abhivādyābhivādyāṃś ca sarvaiś ca pratinanditaḥ
english: Honoured thus by all the sons of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas, saluting and being saluted by all, he was welcomed with joy.

sanskrit: kumāraiḥ sarvaśo vīraḥ satkāreṇābhivāditaḥ samānavayasaḥ sarvān āśliṣya sa punaḥ punaḥ
english: Greeted with honour by princes on all sides, the hero embraced all those of equal age again and again.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇasya bhavane ramye ratnabhojyasamāvṛte uvāsa saha kṛṣṇena bahulās tatra śarvarīḥ
english: In Kṛṣṇa's delightful palace, filled with jewels and rich food, he dwelt together with Kṛṣṇa, passing many nights there.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ katipayāhasya tasmin raivatake girau vṛṣṇyandhakānām abhavat sumahān utsavo nṛpa
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, after a few days, O king, a very great festival of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas took place on that Raivataka mountain.

sanskrit: tatra dānaṃ dadur vīrā brāhmaṇānāṃ sahasraśaḥ bhojavṛṣṇyandhakāś caiva mahe tasya gires tadā
english: There the heroes of the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas gave gifts to brahmins by the thousands, in honour of that great mountain.

sanskrit: prāsādai ratnacitraiś ca gires tasya samantataḥ sa deśaḥ śobhito rājan dīpavṛkṣaiś ca sarvaśaḥ
english: With palaces inlaid with gems all around that mountain, the region was made beautiful, O king, and with lamp-trees on every side.

sanskrit: vāditrāṇi ca tatra sma vādakāḥ samavādayan nanṛtur nartakāś caiva jagur gānāni gāyanāḥ
english: Musicians played their instruments there; dancers danced; and singers sang their songs.

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtāḥ kumārāś ca vṛṣṇīnāṃ sumahaujasaḥ yānair hāṭakacitrāṅgaiś cañcūryante sma sarvaśaḥ
english: Adorned young princes of the Vṛṣṇis, of very great energy, moved about everywhere in carriages decorated with gold ornaments.

sanskrit: paurāś ca pādacāreṇa yānair uccāvacais tathā sadārāḥ sānuyātrāś ca śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Citizens on foot and in vehicles great and small, accompanied by their wives and retinues, moved about in hundreds and thousands.

sanskrit: tato haladharaḥ kṣībo revatīsahitaḥ prabhuḥ anugamyamāno gandharvair acarat tatra bhārata
english: Then Balarama, the wielder of the plough — intoxicated, accompanied by Revati, attended by Gandharvas — roamed there, O Bharata.
